inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K (filed 2026-11-12): cash-flow statement equity-based compensation expense $124m, plus employee equity-based compensation withholding taxes $69m from the statement of shareholders' equity. JCI publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure, so the two lines are summed. Prior years on the same two lines: FY2025 $140m + $34m, FY2024 $107m + $28m.
inputs.share_count_basis: 603.2m = ~601.2m ordinary shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 (605.74m at 2026-06-30 per the Q3 10-Q cover, less 4.56m repurchased in Q4 per the FY2026 10-K Item 5 table; an estimate, the 10-K does not print the September count) plus 2.0m dilutive awards (FY2026 10-K Note 12: basic 609m, diluted 611m weighted). The 10-K cover shows 600.2m at 2026-10-31; the September figure is used so the count matches the 2026-09-30 net debt (October repurchases of ~1m shares, ~$140m, are in neither). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count. JCI is an active repurchaser (FY2026 $1,505m, FY2025 $5,991m including the ~$5bn ASR; $3.2bn authorization remaining), so the flat count is funded, not a modelling convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-29 build. USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.2 x ERP ~4.75% = cost of equity ~9.9%; after-tax cost of debt ~3.9% (avg coupon ~4.8%, 18% cash tax); D/V ~10% at the current market cap. Computed ~9.3%; rounded to 9.0%, the same in every scenario (risk lives in the scenario flows and weights, not the discount rate). The 10-year yield was not re-fetched for this update.
inputs.lease_treatment: ASC 842 operating leases: lease cost is an operating expense already inside the EBITDA margin (treatment B), so operating lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt. total_debt is short-term debt $678m + current LTD $1,066m + LTD $7,533m = $9,277m, per the FY2026 10-K capitalization table.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; noncontrolling interests at book ($35m, 2026-09-30) deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI is immaterial post the Hitachi JV sale (continuing-ops NCI income $10m in FY2026).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical industrial'; adaptations file read for leases, NCI, WC sign and charge-risk-once). UPDATE of the 2026-09-29 build, same model, same 10-year horizon; see `reconciliation` for the bridge and `update_log` for what moved and what was deliberately left alone. FY0 IS NOW AN ACTUAL: FY2026 (year ended 2026-09-30) from the 10-K filed 2026-11-12 and the Q4 earnings release (8-K EX-99.1, 2026-10-27): revenue $25,666m (+8.8% reported, +8% organic; the prior build estimated $25,590m); continuing OCF $3,872m; capex $465m; reported FCF $3,407m (company adjusted FCF $3,229m, 103% conversion); owner FCF $3,214m. Reported FCF carries a net ~$156m AFFF insurance inflow and a working-capital inflow that is not extrapolated (see wc note). All figures are continuing operations; R&LC HVAC (sold to Bosch 2025-07-31) is discontinued throughout and every row FY2022 onward is recast; FY2020-21 in the CSV still include R&LC, so 5-year CAGRs mix bases. EBITDA MARGIN BASIS: pre-SBC (the engine deducts SBC separately) and after a haircut to company adjusted EBITDA for the recurring share of 'non-recurring' restructuring, transformation and transaction costs. FY2026 company adjusted EBITDA $4,743m (18.5% of revenue; 19.0% pre-SBC). FY2026 excluded costs of a cash character: restructuring and related $190m + transformation $292m + transaction/separation $73m = $555m (2.2% of revenue), against the ~1.4pp haircut the prior build used. In Q4 FY2026 the restructuring plan was EXPANDED by $350m to ~$750m through FY2028 (~$400m still to be incurred in FY2027-28), so the haircut is raised to ~1.8pp for FY2027-28 and returns to ~1.4pp from FY2029 once the plan completes. Owner-basis FY2026 margin: ~17.6% on the old 1.4pp haircut (the prior build estimated 17.1%), ~16.8% if all $555m is charged. AFFF insurance recoveries ($149m), the $70m divestiture gain and $73m mark-to-market gains are excluded from the base. Interest income is not stripped: JCI carries $8.7bn net debt and interest income ($8m) is immaterial. Cash tax: adjusted ETR ~17% (Irish plc, Pillar Two floor 15%); FY2026 cash taxes paid ~$655m (kpis table); the FY2026 current provision was $1,334m against a deferred benefit of $798m with accrued income taxes up $679m, so FY2027 cash tax may be lumpy; the 18% -> 20% ramp is unchanged. Working capital: receivables and inventory still exceed payables and deferred revenue on the balance sheet, but FY2026 operating working capital (ex accrued taxes) was a ~$330m INFLOW on +$2.07bn of revenue as deferred revenue rose $900m to $3,370m on data-center customer advances, and FY2027 adjusted FCF conversion is guided ~95% despite capex doubling; wc_capture moved from -5% to 0% (not positive: advances unwind when orders slow). YEAR-ONE CHECK: base FY2027 owner FCF ~$3.29bn (11.6% of revenue) against ~$3.6bn implied by the guide (adjusted EPS midpoint x ~605m shares x 95%, plus after-tax interest, less SBC and withholding); the model sits below guidance because it credits no working-capital inflow. PENDING DIVESTITURES not modelled separately: ADT UK residential security (held for sale, closing FY2027) and Global Intrusion Products (agreed October 2026, closing H1 CY2027); their revenue loss is netted in the FY2027 growth rate, proceeds are not credited. Qualitative context from JCI_Analysis.json (dated 2026-09-29, pre-dates the Q4 print; FY2027 guidance taken from the 8-K directly).

equity_bridge.note: FY2026 10-K balance sheet, 2026-09-30; charged once here, flows are consolidated

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case FY2027-31 average revenue growth (FY2027 guided organic +11-12%; backlog $23.0bn +43% organic; FY2026 orders $29.7bn, +35% organic, book-to-bill ~1.16), decelerating to 3% by FY2035. Equity CAGR is rejected as the anchor: it is negative (-6.2%/yr) purely because buybacks ($6.0bn FY2025, $1.5bn FY2026) and the R&LC carve-out shrank the equity base, and the 5-year revenue CAGR (1.6%) mixes pre- and post-R&LC-divestiture bases.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-6.2% 5yr, -8.3% 3yr) diverges from revenue (+4.75% 3yr, FY2023 $22,331m -> FY2026 $25,666m) and EPS by far more than 30%: the equity base was cut by repurchases and the R&LC carve-out, not by losses. EPS CAGRs are on total reported diluted EPS as carried in the Metrics CSV (FY2023 $2.69, FY2021 $2.27 -> FY2026 $4.68) and so include discontinued R&LC earnings in the start years; on continuing operations the move is steeper (FY2024 $2.08, FY2025 $2.63, FY2026 $4.72). FY2026 GAAP EPS includes ~$0.47 of AFFF recoveries, divestiture and mark-to-market gains; adjusted EPS was $5.16 (+37%). Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR starts from a depressed FY2023 ($1,266m) and is not a run-rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series (continuing OCF - capex - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes; interest income not stripped, net-debt company): FY2020 $1,928m; FY2021 $1,890m; FY2022 $601m; FY2023 $1,266m; FY2024 $943m (depressed by the AFFF settlement and factoring wind-down); FY2025 $1,931m; FY2026 $3,214m. FY2026 is flattered by a working-capital inflow on customer advances and ~$156m of net AFFF insurance cash; the component build does not carry either forward. SBC + withholding has been flat at ~$135-195m/yr, so the owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs agree: SBC is not absorbing the growth.

base.growth_rationale: CHANGED FY2027-28 (was 8.0, 7.0). FY2027 +11.0% reported: guided organic +11-12% less ~0.5-1pp for the ADT UK and Intrusion Products divestitures. FY2028 +8.5%: a $23.0bn backlog (+43% organic), Q4 orders +44% and RPO of $29.3bn extend visibility a second year. FY2029 onward UNCHANGED: a bigger order peak raises the size of an eventual digestion as much as it extends the run.
base.margin_rationale: CHANGED (was 17.5 rising to 19.5). Pre-SBC, post-haircut owner EBITDA margin. FY2027 18.2%: guided adjusted EPS $6.15-6.30 implies adjusted EBIT ~17.1% and adjusted EBITDA ~19.5% (~20.0% pre-SBC), less a 1.8pp haircut. Mature level raised 19.5% -> 20.0%, reached FY2033: the FY2026 actual came in ~0.45pp above the estimate the old path was built from, and the same climb is preserved from the higher base. Company-basis equivalent ~21% adjusted EBITDA; guided 30%+ operating leverage held for three years would exceed this, so the base assumes leverage fades after FY2029.
base.da_rationale: UNCHANGED. FY2026 D&A $654m, 2.55% of revenue (amortisation of intangibles $351m), in line with the prior estimate; only the tax-deductible share is carried. The FY2027-28 capex step-up will add depreciation later; not modelled, which slightly understates the tax shield.
base.capex_rationale: CHANGED FY2027-30 (was 1.5-1.6 throughout). The FY2026 10-K states ~$900m of FY2027 capex (FY2026 $465m, 1.8%) to expand thermal-management capacity: 3.2% of FY2027 revenue, tapering to the unchanged 1.6% run-rate by FY2031.
base.tax_rationale: UNCHANGED. Adjusted ETR ~17% in FY2026; cash rate ramps 18% -> 20% for Pillar Two and the historical cash-over-book gap.
base.wc_rationale: CHANGED -5% -> 0%. FY2026 operating working capital was an inflow on customer advances; see inputs.notes.

bull.narrative: Guidance is beaten again (it was raised at every FY2026 report): +13%/+11%/+9% for FY2027-29 as the backlog converts and orders keep coming, margins reach Trane-class 21.5% (owner basis) two years earlier than the prior build, capacity capex stays elevated through FY2029, tax holds near the guided 17-19%. CHANGED: growth FY2027-28 (was 11, 10), margin path pulled forward (terminal 21.5% unchanged), capex FY2027-31. UNCHANGED: growth FY2029+, tax, terminal growth, cap.

bear.narrative: The backlog makes FY2027 largely visible even here (+8%, below the guide), but the data-center wave is a capex cycle: orders roll over during FY2028 (+3%) and revenue falls 4% in FY2029 as hyperscalers digest, with the $900m of FY2027 capacity capex already spent; margins slip to 15.8% as operating leverage reverses and recover only to 17%; restructuring and transformation stay permanent; cash tax settles at 21%. CHANGED: growth FY2027-29 (was 4, 2, -3: a higher peak and a deeper trough), margins FY2027-30 from the higher FY2026 actual (terminal 17.0% unchanged), capex FY2027-28. UNCHANGED: growth FY2030+, tax, terminal growth, cap.

scenario_narratives.base: JCI's axes are (1) how long the AI data-center cooling wave sustains the order book, (2) whether the Danaher-style operating system turns 30%+ operating leverage into a durable margin step-up, and (3) how much of the perennial restructuring and transformation spend is truly non-recurring. Base: the $23.0bn backlog delivers +11% in FY2027 (guided +11-12% organic, less divestitures) and +8.5% in FY2028, then growth fades to 3% by FY2035 as hyperscaler capex normalises and EMEA/APAC stay low-to-mid single digit; owner EBITDA margin (pre-SBC, after a 1.4-1.8pp haircut for recurring 'one-off' charges) rises from ~17.6% in FY2026 to 18.2% in FY2027 and 20.0% by FY2033; capex doubles to ~$900m (3.2%) in FY2027 for thermal capacity and tapers to 1.6%; working capital is neutral; cash tax 18% -> 20%. Terminal 2.5% growth at 9% WACC (Gordon ~15.8x binds below the 17x cap).
scenario_narratives.bull: Hyperscaler and AI-factory demand persists through the decade and JCI's chiller, CDU and liquid-cooling share (Alloy Enterprises acquired FY2026) holds against Trane and Carrier: revenue compounds +13%/+11%/+9% for FY2027-29 and is still growing 5% in FY2033; the business system takes owner EBITDA margin to 21.5% (company basis ~23%) by FY2033, the restructuring haircut effectively disappearing into productivity after the plan ends in FY2028; cash tax stays near the guided 17-19% Irish-plc rate; terminal 3.0% with a 19x cap (Gordon ~17.2x binds).
scenario_narratives.bear: The data-center thesis is a capex cycle and the 10-K now names the dependency on 'a limited number of hyperscale technology companies' as a risk factor: FY2027 is carried by backlog (+8%), orders roll over in FY2028 and revenue falls 4% in FY2029, with China and EMEA still soft and new capacity under-absorbed; margins slip back toward 15.8% as operating leverage reverses before recovering only to 17%; restructuring and transformation stay permanent; asbestos/AFFF and tariff costs bite; cash tax settles at 21%. Terminal 2.0% with a 15x cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 20/50/30 (house default is 15/50/35). Bear stays at 20%: the growth story is concentrated on one identifiable cycle, AI data-center capex, and the Q4 print made that concentration larger, not smaller (Americas orders +58%, the company is now committing $900m of capacity capex to it); a digestion phase is a real, dated downside axis. Bull stays at 30%: it needs sustained hyperscaler spend AND full delivery of a multi-year margin program while Trane and Carrier attack the same niche. Base at 50%. The balance sheet (1.8x net debt/adjusted EBITDA, BBB+/Baa1 stable) carries no solvency element, so the bear is a cyclical earnings path, not a going-concern case. What would move the weights: two consecutive quarters of organic orders below sales growth (bear up), or FY2027 delivered at or above the guide with backlog still growing 20%+ (bull up).

Bull 21.5% and bear 17.0% mature margins; lease and NCI treatment; model choice.

valuation_philosophy.summary: JCI is valued as a cyclical industrial compounder on owner FCF: continuing-ops cash flow after SBC and equity-award taxes, with the company's 'adjusted' EBITDA haircut for the recurring share of restructuring and transformation costs, discounted at a single 9% USD WACC, with leases as operating cost, NCI charged once in the bridge, and a terminal value that never exceeds the 17x cap. The FY2026 print and FY2027 guide were both stronger than the September build assumed and the value moved up with them, but the market price still sits close to the bull case; the model's job is to say what the backlog and the margin program are worth to a buyer demanding a 15% return and to show, via the required-return table, what return the market price actually implies on the base path.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI data-center capex digestion: orders (+35% FY2026, +44% Q4) and backlog (+43%) are the growth evidence, and the company is now adding ~$900m of capacity against them; a hyperscaler pause removes the FY2027-28 growth years and strands that capacity.

The restructuring/transformation haircut (1.8pp FY2027-28, 1.4pp after) is a judgment: FY2026 excluded cash-type costs were $555m (2.2% of revenue) and the plan was just expanded; charging the full 2.2pp in perpetuity would cost roughly $5/share on the base case, while a genuine end after FY2028 would add roughly $8.
Working capital: wc_capture was moved from -5% to 0% on one year of customer-advance inflows; reverting it costs ~$1.7/share of weighted value, and advances reverse if orders fall.

Cash tax: an Irish plc guiding ~17%; the FY2026 current provision ($1.33bn) ran far ahead of cash paid (~$0.66bn), so FY2027 cash tax may spike; a US or OECD challenge to the structure would cost more.

Legacy asbestos and AFFF liabilities are outside the bridge (asbestos largely funded by restricted investments; AFFF settlement paid, insurance recoveries still arriving); a further adverse ruling would be a direct deduction.
Pending divestitures (ADT UK residential, Global Intrusion Products) are netted in growth but their proceeds are not credited; small relative to the equity value.
Terminal value is 53-61% of enterprise value; a 1pp change in WACC moves the base value by roughly 15%.
